title: INNIO books 450 MW firm order for Jenbacher J624 gas engines for US data-centre prime power
description: INNIO announced a 450 MW order from an undisclosed US energy company for containerized Jenbacher J624 gas engines to support behind-the-meter prime power for large-scale data centres in North America. The order was booked in Q3 2026 and the engines are expected to be delivered by 2028.
quote: data center developers are seeking on-site and behind-the-meter power solutions that can be delivered independently of the growing grid constraints in North America
analysis: Gas-engine prime power for data centres is being booked years ahead (delivery by 2028), which signals tight engine and container supply that Gulf data-centre buyers will also compete for. Action: confirm with Cummins which 2027-28 gas genset production slots can be reserved for Gulf data-centre bids before quoting delivery dates.

title: HD Construction Equipment signs KRW 390 billion deal to supply gas engines for US hyperscale data-centre gensets
description: South Korea's HD Construction Equipment signed a 390 billion won (USD 291.4 million) agreement with US firm ERock to supply 22-liter long-block gas engines from 2027 through 2028. ERock will build them into generator sets for hyperscale data centres run by US tech companies.
quote: ERock will integrate the partially assembled engines into generator sets to supply power to hyperscale data centers operated by US tech companies
analysis: A new Asian engine maker is entering the data-centre genset supply chain for 2027-28, which adds engine supply but also a new low-cost engine brand that could later reach Gulf packagers. Action: add HD Construction Equipment / ERock to the competitor watchlist and check whether they plan any Middle East channel.

title: Cushman & Wakefield: Americas data-centre construction hits a record 37.7 GW, 91.7% precommitted, vacancy 3.8%
description: Cushman & Wakefield's H1 2026 Americas Data Center Update reports a record 37.7 GW under construction, with 50.3 GW operational and another 285 GW in the planned pipeline. Vacancy has fallen to 3.8% and access to power and infrastructure is increasingly determining where growth can occur.
quote: Capacity under construction is 91.7 percent precommitted, while region-wide vacancy has fallen to just 3.8 percent
analysis: Near-fully precommitted construction shows sustained global demand for backup and prime power, which supports Cummins' order book but also means US projects absorb large-genset production that Gulf projects need. Action: ask Cummins for allocation visibility on 2.5 MW+ gensets for pending Gulf data-centre awards.

title: JLL: Asia-Pacific data-centre capacity to nearly double from 32 GW to 57 GW by 2030, grid connections a bottleneck
description: JLL expects Asia-Pacific data-centre capacity to rise from 32 GW today to 57 GW by 2030. The article notes grid congestion spreading across the US, Europe and Asia-Pacific, with data-centre construction outpacing grid planning in several Asian markets.
quote: the data centre capacity in Asia-Pacific is expected to nearly double from 32GW today to 57GW by 2030
analysis: A near-doubling of regional capacity means a large Asian backup and prime-power market that competes with the Gulf for genset supply but confirms the growth thesis Cummins Arabia is selling. Action: use the JLL growth figure in data-centre pitch material as third-party evidence of demand.

title: Fitch unit BMI: grid capacity limits across Asia are binding as AI and data-centre demand rises
description: BMI, a Fitch research unit, raised its 10-year electricity consumption forecasts for Thailand (2.9%), Malaysia (3.3%) and Vietnam (5.6%) a year, mainly on data-centre investment and AI workloads. It said regulatory tightening in Thailand, Malaysia and Australia is limiting grid-connected load growth and expects a resurgence in thermal power.
quote: Grid capacity constraints across Asia are becoming increasingly binding as rising electricity demand from artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres puts pressure on power systems
analysis: Where grids cannot connect data centres quickly, regulators and developers lean on dispatchable thermal capacity, which favours on-site gas and diesel power suppliers. Action: reference the Asian grid-limit pattern when pitching on-site prime and backup power for Gulf campuses.

title: TrendForce: global data-centre power demand to reach 161 GW in 2026, up 31%, with a 268 GW grid supply gap by 2030
description: TrendForce estimates global data-centre power demand capacity at 161 GW in 2026, up about 31% year on year, and 490.7 GW by 2030 against only 222.6 GW of grid capacity available to data centres. It notes the 268 GW gap excludes behind-the-meter on-site generation, so the real shortage may be smaller.
quote: TrendForce estimates that global data center power demand capacity will reach 161 GW in 2026, up approximately 31% YoY.
analysis: The 268 GW gap is TrendForce's own estimate, but the page itself says on-site generation could offset part of it, which supports demand for gensets as grid delays persist. Action: cite the TrendForce 161 GW and 268 GW figures, labelled as TrendForce estimates, in data-centre pitch material.

title: Amsterdam data-centre vacancy falls to 2.7% as grid connection moratorium freezes new capacity until about 2029
description: Datacentres.com Research reports Amsterdam vacancy at 2.7%, the tightest in Europe, with 1,340 MW live. It says TenneT's queue shows roughly 4.6 GW of unmet demand with no headroom until new 380kV infrastructure around 2029.
quote: TenneT's transmission queue showing roughly 4.6 GW of unmet demand against zero available headroom until new 380kV infrastructure completes around 2029
analysis: Grid access, not demand, is the limiting factor in a mature hub, per Datacentres.com Research (figures not independently verified). Action: where Gulf utility connection dates slip, offer bridging or prime power in data-centre bids and confirm the connection timeline with the utility first.

title: New York/New Jersey: diesel backup faces stricter NYC air permitting as operators turn to gas turbines and fuel cells for new builds
description: Datacentres.com Research reports about 1,120 MW live in the New York/New Jersey market, with PSE&G interconnection study-to-energisation times of 42-54 months for projects above 50 MW. It says diesel backup faces stricter NYC air permitting, pushing some operators toward behind-the-meter gas turbines or fuel cells.
quote: Diesel backup generation, long the default resiliency layer for Manhattan facilities, faces increasingly restrictive New York City Department of Environmental Protection air permitting
analysis: Air-permit limits on diesel in dense US metros are steering some new builds to turbines and fuel cells, a substitution risk for diesel gensets that the page ties to NYC, not to the Gulf. Action: keep gas and dual-fuel genset options ready in Cummins Arabia data-centre offers in case Gulf permitting follows.

title: Hitachi and Bloom Energy team up on fuel-cell on-site power for data centres and industry in Japan
description: Hitachi announced a collaboration with Bloom Energy to deliver fuel-cell-based on-site power for data centres and industrial customers in Japan. Hitachi will lead planning, design and operational support and Bloom will supply the fuel cells.
quote: Hitachi will accelerate the deployment of on-site power solutions for data centers and industrial facilities by combining its control and system integration capabilities with Bloom Energy's fuel cell technology.
analysis: A large systems integrator is packaging fuel cells as on-site data-centre power, a non-genset alternative backed by an established industrial channel. Action: track whether Hitachi or Bloom offer fuel-cell packages to Gulf data-centre developers and prepare a genset-versus-fuel-cell comparison.
